routes.name: Walk 1: Chipping Campden and Dover's Hill
routes.description: Through the market town past the 1627 Market Hall, Lynches Wood and up Dover's Hill, home of the Cotswold Olimpick Games. Some steep sections; a 3-mile short-cut variant avoids the climbs.
routes.startLocation: Back Ends, Chipping Campden (free parking)

routes.name: Walk 2: Broadway and the Tower
routes.description: From Broadway's high street up historic tracks to Broadway Tower (1798), passing St Eadburgha's Church, with views across the Severn Vale into Wales. Now stile-free following route improvements; some steep sections.
routes.startLocation: Broadway village (three car parks; pin: Church Close)

routes.name: Walk 3: Stanton, Snowshill and the Edge
routes.description: Links the picture-postcard villages of Stanton and Snowshill over hilltops and woodland, passing Shenberrow Hill Camp and Snowshill Manor. Stiles, steep sections and mud after wet weather.
routes.startLocation: Stanton Village Club car park, by the cricket ground

routes.name: Walk 3 (short): Stanton and Shenberrow Hill Fort
routes.description: Short loop from Stanton up to the Iron Age Shenberrow Hill Camp and back. Stiles and steep sections; muddy after wet weather.
routes.startLocation: Stanton Village Club car park, by the cricket ground

routes.name: Walk 4: Winchcombe and Belas Knap
routes.description: From Winchcombe along old and new Cotswold Way routes up to Belas Knap Neolithic long barrow, with views over Sudeley Castle. Steep sections and stiles; a 3.5-mile short-cut is available.
routes.startLocation: Back Lane car park, Winchcombe (GL54 5PZ)

routes.name: Walk 5: Cleeve Hill Common Ring
routes.description: A ring around Cleeve Common — the Cotswolds' largest common and highest point — over limestone grassland past The Twins, the Single Beech and Prestbury Hill Butterfly Reserve. No stiles; some steep sections.
routes.startLocation: Old quarry car park by Cleeve Hill golf club

routes.name: Walk 5 (shorter): Cleeve Hill Common
routes.description: Shorter, mostly level loop of Cleeve Common's limestone grassland with views to the Malverns and Black Mountains. Published as easy: no stiles, mostly level.
routes.startLocation: Old quarry car park by Cleeve Hill golf club

routes.name: Walk 6: Leckhampton Loop — Seven Springs and the Devil's Chimney
routes.description: Loops Leckhampton Hill and Charlton Kings Common, visiting Seven Springs (a claimed source of the Thames), an Iron Age hillfort and the Devil's Chimney rock pinnacle. No stiles; some steep sections.
routes.startLocation: Lay-by opposite the Seven Springs pub

routes.name: Walk 7: Cranham, Coopers and the Beechwoods
routes.description: Through Buckholt Wood and the Cotswold Commons and Beechwoods National Nature Reserve to Cooper's Hill, site of the famous cheese-rolling. No stiles; some moderately steep sections.
routes.startLocation: Cranham village (parking outside the village or at Buckholt Wood)

routes.name: Walk 8: The Selsley Circuit — Commons and Canals
routes.description: Follows the National Trail for nearly all its length over Selsley Common and along the Stroudwater Canal past Ebley Mill and All Saints Church with its Morris & Co windows. Three stiles and some steep sections.
routes.startLocation: King's Stanley Village Hall

routes.name: Walk 9: Cam Long Down and Uley — Hills and Hillforts
routes.description: Climbs Uley Bury hillfort, Downham 'Smallpox' Hill and the twin peaks of Cam Peak and Cam Long Down, with views over the Severn Estuary into Wales. Stiles, steps and steep sections.
routes.startLocation: The Old Crown, Uley (customer parking; bus 65 from Stroud)

routes.name: Walk 9 (short): Uley Bury Hillfort
routes.description: Short circuit of the ramparts of Uley Bury, a 13-hectare Iron Age hillfort of about 300 BC. Steps and steep sections.
routes.startLocation: The Old Crown, Uley (customer parking)

routes.name: Walk 10: Wotton-under-Edge and Wortley Hill
routes.description: From the Tolsey Clock over farmland and woodland tracks to Wortley Hill, with optional detours to Blackquarries Hill Long Barrow and Newark Park. Stiles and steep sections.
routes.startLocation: Wotton-under-Edge (three free car parks; pin: The Chipping)

routes.name: Walk 11: Old Sodbury — The Hillfort and Church
routes.description: Follows the Cotswold Way up to 13th-century St John's Church and around the double ramparts of Sodbury Iron Age hillfort with views over the Severn Vale. No stiles; steepish slopes.
routes.startLocation: Old Sodbury (free parking along Chapel Lane)

routes.name: Walk 12: Journey's End — The Walk into Bath
routes.description: A linear finale following the trail from Lansdown past Prospect Stile, Royal Victoria Park and the Royal Crescent to the Cotswold Way marker stone at Bath Abbey. Return by bus 31. One stile; some steep sections.
routes.startLocation: Lansdown Park & Ride, Bath (BA1 9BJ)

routes.name: Walk 13: Stinchcombe Hill — Korea Friendship Trail
routes.description: A loop of Stinchcombe Hill twinned with Route 3 of South Korea's Jeju Olle Trail. Firm surface and no stiles, with one long steep ascent and descent; a 3-mile hill-only variant is easy and mostly level.
routes.startLocation: Stinchcombe Hill car park (GL11 6AQ) or Dursley town car parks

routes.name: Walk 14: Haresfield — Bruce Trail Friendship Trail
routes.description: Stile-free loop over Haresfield Beacon, Standish Wood, Cromwell's Stone and Rudge Hill, twinned with Ontario's Bruce Trail. Moderate slopes.
routes.startLocation: Shortwood National Trust car park, Haresfield (charges apply — pin marks Haresfield Beacon; see official guide for directions)

routes.name: Walk 15: Hailes Abbey and Beckbury Camp
routes.description: Up a monks' track to Beckbury Camp hillfort and 'Cromwell's Seat', returning past Hailes Church and the ruins of Hailes Abbey. Some steep sections and two stiles.
routes.startLocation: Hayles Fruit Farm, Hailes

routes.name: Walk 16: Stinchcombe Hill — Leaf & Ground
routes.description: A traverse of Stinchcombe Hill with Severn Vale views, descending on hard paths to the Leaf and Ground cafe. 144m of ascent; suitable for families but not pushchairs or buggies.
routes.startLocation: Stinchcombe Hill car park (GL11 6AQ)

routes.name: Winchcombe to the source of the River Isbourne
routes.description: Cotswold Gateways route from Winchcombe to the Isbourne's source, passing the 1897 sheep Washpool at 'Watery Bottom'.
routes.startLocation: Back Lane car park, Winchcombe (GL54 5PZ)

routes.name: Winchcombe, Hailes Abbey and Farmcote
routes.description: Loop from Winchcombe via the Hailes Abbey ruins and the Saxon-origin St Faith's Church and herb garden at Farmcote.
routes.startLocation: Back Lane car park, Winchcombe (GL54 5PZ)

routes.name: Dursley Figure of Eight — Western Loop
routes.description: West around Dursley through fields, woods and the Stinchcombe Hill golf course with panoramic views and Racklease Nature Reserve. A sustained climb early on; one descent can be muddy and uneven.
routes.startLocation: May Lane car park, Dursley

routes.name: Wotton-under-Edge: Brackenbury Ditches, Tyndale Monument and Westridge Woods
routes.description: Via the Jubilee Clump on Wotton Hill, Brackenbury Ditches hillfort and the Tyndale Monument above North Nibley.
routes.startLocation: Wotton-under-Edge (three free car parks)

routes.name: Wotton-under-Edge via Tyley Bottom, Ozleworth and Newark Park
routes.description: Through Tyley Bottom and Ozleworth to National Trust Newark Park. Paths can be uneven and muddy; a shorter variant is in the official guide.
routes.startLocation: Wotton-under-Edge (three free car parks)

routes.name: Wotton-under-Edge via Wortley, Tor Hill, Combe Hill and Wotton Hill
routes.description: Circuit via Wortley, Tor Hill, Combe Hill and the Waterloo and Jubilee trees on Wotton Hill, with an optional detour to Blackquarries Hill Long Barrow. Paths can be uneven and muddy.
routes.startLocation: Wotton-under-Edge (three free car parks)

routes.name: Hawkesbury Upton and Kilcott
routes.description: Through fields and woods via Kilcott with views of Newark Park, passing the 1846 Somerset Monument. One steep climb.
routes.startLocation: Hawkesbury Upton Village Hall car park

routes.name: Hawkesbury Upton via the Church of St Mary the Virgin
routes.description: To the pre-Norman Church of St Mary the Virgin below Hawkesbury Knoll and its chambered long barrow. One steep climb and a few stiles.
routes.startLocation: Hawkesbury Upton Village Hall car park

routes.name: Marshfield, Cold Ashton, Doynton, Dyrham and West Littleton
routes.description: A long link of Marshfield, Cold Ashton, Doynton, National Trust Dyrham Park and the historic bell tower of St James, West Littleton. Lengthy, with several climbs.
routes.startLocation: Withymead Recreation Ground, Marshfield (SN14 8PB)

routes.name: Winchcombe — Miles without Stiles
routes.description: A stile-free loop from Winchcombe on unsurfaced paths. Public toilets in the Back Lane car park.
routes.startLocation: Back Lane car park, Winchcombe (GL54 5PW)

accessibility.summary: Unsurfaced paths, basic fitness. Stile free — these routes do not have stiles, but may have kissing gates or footbridges, and/or steep, narrow or muddy sections.

routes.name: Winchcombe and the Sudeley Valley — Miles without Stiles
routes.description: A longer stile-free loop through the Sudeley Valley below Winchcombe. Toilets next to the library in the Back Lane car park.
routes.startLocation: Cowl Lane, Winchcombe (GL54 5RA)

accessibility.summary: May be steep slopes, moderate fitness. Stile free — may have kissing gates or footbridges, and/or steep, narrow or muddy sections.

routes.name: Winchcombe's 'Ultimate' Walk on Wheels
routes.description: An eight-and-a-half-mile circuit around Winchcombe designed for all-terrain (off-road) mobility scooters. Disabled public toilets in the Back Lane car park.
routes.startLocation: Back Lane car park, Winchcombe (GL54 5PZ)

accessibility.summary: The route is on grass, field edges, stone and tarmac with long slopes to and from the Salt Way. Designed for off-road mobility scooters (trampers); stile free.

routes.name: Broadway Village — Miles without Stiles
routes.description: A short stile-free loop around Broadway village on unsurfaced paths. Toilets at the short-stay car park and the Activity Park.
routes.startLocation: The Clock, Broadway (WR12 7DT)

accessibility.summary: Unsurfaced paths, basic fitness. Stile free — may have kissing gates or footbridges, and/or steep, narrow or muddy sections.

routes.name: Laverton to Buckland — Walks on Wheels
routes.description: An easy there-and-back path between Laverton and Buckland below the escarpment, published as suitable for all wheels. Nearest accessible toilets at Church Close, Broadway.
routes.startLocation: Laverton, near Broadway (WR12 7NA)

accessibility.summary: An easy there and back path of 1.6 miles on stone and tarmac with very gentle ascent and descent, suitable for all wheels. Rated: stile free, pushchair friendly, mobility scooter, wheelchair friendly.

routes.name: Dover's Hill — Walks on Wheels
routes.description: A short grassy walk on the plateau of Dover's Hill above Chipping Campden. The main quarter-mile stretch is level and suitable for all; a longer loop has steep slopes. Accessible toilets in Sheep Street, Chipping Campden.
routes.startLocation: Dover's Hill car park (National Trust, GL55 6UW)

accessibility.summary: Grassy level walk 0.25 miles suitable for all; extra loop has steep slopes. The surface is mostly grass with some uneven patches — after rain there will be puddles, and it is grazed by sheep.

routes.name: Crickley Hill — Walks on Wheels
routes.description: A short accessible route at Crickley Hill Country Park, where a Tramper all-terrain scooter can also be hired from Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust. Accessible toilets and refreshments at the visitor centre.
routes.startLocation: Crickley Hill Country Park visitor centre (GL4 8JY)

accessibility.summary: The surface is tarmac, crushed stone, short grass and earth. Rated pushchair friendly; short but uneven grass for 30 metres, and an optional short moderate climb on a hard surface.

routes.name: Leckhampton Hill mobility scooter route
routes.description: The Cotswold Voluntary Wardens' 50th Anniversary project: a mobility-scooter route following sections of the Cotswold Way on Leckhampton Hill. Accessible toilets at the Wildlife Trust cafe at Crickley Hill.
routes.startLocation: Brownstones Quarry car park, Hartley Lane (near Star Bistro, GL53 9QU)

accessibility.summary: A mix of hard or grassy and mostly flat surface accessible by any reasonably sturdy mobility scooter. Can be muddy after rain. Gradients do not exceed 10% and there are no significant cross gradients. Pushchair friendly.

routes.name: Leckhampton Hill and Charlton Kings Common — Miles without Stiles
routes.description: A stile-free circuit of Leckhampton Hill and Charlton Kings Common using part of the Cotswold Way National Trail — the only circular route here with an official GPX line, shown on the map.
routes.startLocation: Daisy Bank car park, off Leckhampton Hill (SO949188)

accessibility.summary: May be steep slopes, moderate fitness. Stile free. Warning from the publisher: the steep path is now scoured out and not suitable for mobility scooters, trampers or push chairs.

routes.name: Cleeve Common South — Walks on Wheels
routes.description: A short route on the southern plateau of Cleeve Common, starting almost level by the masts with longer extensions over uneven ground.
routes.startLocation: Cleeve Common car park by the masts (SO994248)

accessibility.summary: The 600 metre route is almost level, while the longer routes cross uneven ground with several slopes. Pushchair friendly; suitable for all-terrain mobility scooters and mountain buggies, though wheelchairs and small wheels may find the longer extensions difficult.

routes.name: Painswick Beacon — Miles without Stiles
routes.description: A stile-free loop of Painswick Beacon following the signposted Cotswold Way along the eastern side of the Iron Age fort.
routes.startLocation: Parking area at the end of the road to the Beacon, off Cheltenham Road (GL6 6TU)

accessibility.summary: May be steep slopes, moderate fitness. Stile free — may have kissing gates or footbridges, and/or steep, narrow or muddy sections.

routes.name: King's Stanley to Ebley Mill — Miles without Stiles
routes.description: A stile-free walk between King's Stanley and Ebley Mill incorporating sections of the Cotswold Way along the Stroudwater canal corridor.
routes.startLocation: King's Head, King's Stanley (GL10 3JB; free parking at the playing fields)

accessibility.summary: Unsurfaced paths, basic fitness. Stile free — these routes do not have stiles, but may have kissing gates or footbridges, and/or steep, narrow or muddy sections.

accessibleSections.name: The Cotswold Way as a whole
accessibleSections.description: The National Trail is explicit that the full trail is not accessible: "the trail is not stile free and does pass over farm land that will have livestock (including sheep, cows and horses) freely grazing." No official body currently certifies any section of the Cotswold Way as wheelchair-accessible — the entries below are what IS published.

accessibleSections.name: Leckhampton Hill — improved access section
accessibleSections.description: "Several sections of the Cotswold Way have been improved to provide access for people with restricted mobility, including at Leckhampton." The Cotswold Voluntary Wardens' 2.25-mile mobility scooter route here follows sections of the trail (see the route card).

accessibleSections.name: Crickley Hill — Tramper hire on the Cotswold Way
accessibleSections.description: "There are several places suitable for those with restricted mobility, and even an off road mobility scooter for hire to explore the Cotswold Way around Crickley Hill Country Park, through Countryside Mobility." Tramper hire from Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust (01452 383333); Blue Badge parking and accessible toilets at the visitor centre.
accessibleSections.startLocation: Crickley Hill Country Park visitor centre
